peigneur/1.script: Imagine working on an oil rig... when the entire lake beneath you starts disappearing.
peigneur/1.heard: Imagine working on an oil rig when the entire lake beneath you starts disappearing.

peigneur/2.script: The water begins to spin. And the rig starts to tilt.
peigneur/2.heard: The water begins to spin, and the rig starts to tilt.

peigneur/3.script: This is Lake Peigneur, in Louisiana. November twentieth, nineteen eighty.
peigneur/3.heard: This is Lake Peñor in Louisiana, November 20th, 1980.

peigneur/4.script: The lake was only ten feet deep. But beneath it was a giant salt mine.
peigneur/4.heard: The lake was only 10 feet deep, but beneath it was a giant salt mine.

peigneur/5.script: That morning, an oil drill got stuck more than twelve hundred feet down.
peigneur/5.heard: That morning, an oil drill got stuck more than 1,200 feet down.

peigneur/6.script: It had punched straight into the mine.
peigneur/6.heard: it had punched straight into the mime.

peigneur/7.script: Water poured in, dissolving the salt pillars that held the tunnels up.
peigneur/7.heard: water poured in, dissolving the salt pillars that held the tunnels up

peigneur/8.script: The hole grew wider... and the lake drained, like a giant bathtub.
peigneur/8.heard: The hole grew wider and the lake drained like a giant bathtub.

peigneur/9.script: A whirlpool swallowed the rig, a tugboat, eleven barges, and part of an island.
peigneur/9.heard: A whirlpool swallowed the rig, a tugboat, 11 barges, and part of an island.

peigneur/10.script: Even a nearby canal flowed backwards, into a hundred-and-sixty-foot waterfall.
peigneur/10.heard: Even a nearby canal flowed backwards into a 160-foot waterfall.

peigneur/12.script: All seven men on the rig escaped. So did all fifty-five miners.
peigneur/12.heard: All seven men on the rig escaped, so did all 55 miners.

peigneur/13.script: Nobody was killed. But when the lake refilled... it was salt water.
peigneur/13.heard: Nobody was killed, but when the lake refilled, it was salt water.

molasses/1.script: Imagine walking down the street... when a giant wave of thick, sticky liquid comes rushing toward you.
molasses/1.heard: Imagine walking down the street when a giant wave of thick, sticky liquid comes rushing toward you.

molasses/4.script: On the waterfront stood a fifty-foot steel tank, holding over two million gallons of molasses.
molasses/4.heard: On the waterfront stood a 50-foot steel tank holding over 2 million gallons of molasses.

molasses/5.script: It leaked so badly, it was painted brown to hide the stains.
molasses/5.heard: It leaked so badly, it was painted brown to hide the stains.

molasses/6.script: Then the rivets started popping, like gunfire... and the tank burst apart.
molasses/6.heard: Then the rivet started popping like gunfire and the tank burst apart.

molasses/7.script: A wave up to twenty-five feet high tore through the streets at around thirty-five miles an hour.
molasses/7.heard: A wave up to 25 feet high tore through the streets at around 35 miles an hour.

molasses/8.script: It crushed buildings, and twisted the steel of an elevated railway.
molasses/8.heard: It crushed buildings and twisted the steel of an elevated railway.

molasses/9.script: And here's what made it so deadly. In the freezing air, the molasses thickened like glue.
molasses/9.heard: And here's what made it so deadly.  In the freezing air, the molasses thicken like glue.

molasses/10.script: Anyone caught in it couldn't escape.
molasses/10.heard: Anyone caught in it couldn't escape.

molasses/11.script: Sailors, police and Red Cross nurses waded in to help.
molasses/11.heard: Sailors, police, and Red Cross nurses waited in to help.

molasses/12.script: Twenty-one people died. About a hundred and fifty were injured.

molasses/13.script: It sounds unbelievable. But it was real... and it changed building safety rules for good.
molasses/13.heard: It sounds unbelievable, but it was real and it changed building safety rules for good.

sinkhole/1.script: Imagine falling asleep in your own bed... and the ground beneath your bedroom opens up.
sinkhole/1.heard: Imagine falling asleep in your own bed, and the ground beneath your bedroom opens up.

sinkhole/2.script: Seffner, Florida. February twenty-eighth, twenty thirteen. Around eleven at night.
sinkhole/2.heard: Sefner, Florida, February 28, 2013, around 11 at night.

sinkhole/3.script: The family was getting ready for bed, when a loud crash rang out.

sinkhole/4.script: Jeremy Bush ran to his brother Jeff's bedroom... and the room was gone.
sinkhole/4.heard: Jeremy Bush ran to his brother Jeff's bedroom and the room was gone.

sinkhole/5.script: Jeff, and everything in his room, had dropped into a hole thirty feet wide.
sinkhole/5.heard: Jeff and everything in his room had dropped into a hole 30 feet wide.

sinkhole/6.script: Jeremy jumped in, digging desperately, calling his brother's name.

sinkhole/7.script: But the floor kept collapsing. A sheriff's deputy reached in, and pulled him out.

sinkhole/8.script: So how does the ground just... vanish?
sinkhole/8.heard: So how does the ground just...vanish?

sinkhole/9.script: Much of Florida sits on limestone, and rainwater slowly eats it away, leaving hidden caverns.

sinkhole/10.script: The soil above can hold... until suddenly, it can't.

sinkhole/11.script: Rescuers searched, but the ground was too unstable. Jeff's body was never recovered.

sinkhole/12.script: And here's the haunting part. That same sinkhole has opened up again. Twice.
